title: NY State Assembly · District 86
area: West Bronx, including University Heights, Morris Heights, Mount Eden, Kingsbridge, Tremont and Fordham.

context.text: Incumbent Yudelka Tapia is unopposed in the Democratic primary. Maria Diaz defeated Shery Olivo 57.5%-35.8% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary; Olivo separately advanced unopposed on the Conservative Party line, so both remain on the November ballot.

candidates.name: Yudelka Tapia

summary.text: Yudelka Tapia is the Democratic nominee for re-election in NY Assembly District 86, a West Bronx seat she has held since November 2021. A former New York City Comptroller's office auditor and union leader, she serves on the Banks, Corporations, Economic Development, Housing, Labor and Mental Health committees.

background.text: Born in Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic; immigrated to the West Bronx more than 30 years ago and raised four sons there in New York City public schools.
Attended O&M University in Santo Domingo, where she organized fellow students against domestic violence and political corruption and served as president of the Unión Democrática de Mujeres.
Earned a Master of Science in Urban Policy and Leadership from Hunter College.
Worked for 23 years as a Senior Auditor for the New York City Comptroller's Office.
Served as PTA President at Roosevelt High School and as an executive committee member for the local 1407-DC 37 union.

priorities.text: A just recovery from COVID-19 that uplifts working families, communities of color and immigrants, including support for small businesses.
Preserving and expanding affordable housing, including building 100% sustainable permanent affordable housing and reforming the 421-a tax program.
Protecting tenants by stopping evictions, building on the state's rent regulations, and holding bad landlords accountable.
Fighting for NYCHA residents through major infrastructural investment without privatization.

positions.summary: Says she will fight to stop evictions, build upon the state's rent regulations, hold bad landlords accountable, and protect tenants from discrimination and harassment.

candidates.researchNotes: Tapia has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, and her sponsored-legislation table on Ballotpedia is rendered via JavaScript and was not accessible to this research tool. Her campaign website's issues page appears to date from an earlier campaign cycle (its language centers on COVID-19 recovery) but is her most recent publicly available statement of positions found; no distinct 2026-specific platform page or official record of sponsored bills could be located.

candidates.name: Maria Diaz

summary.text: Maria Diaz is the Republican nominee for NY Assembly District 86, having defeated Shery Olivo in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary. She has not previously held elected office.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website, Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response, biography, or public policy statements could be located for Diaz beyond her primary-election result. She has not held elected office.

candidates.name: Shery Olivo

summary.text: Shery Olivo is the Conservative Party nominee for NY Assembly District 86, after losing the Republican primary to Maria Diaz. Born in the Dominican Republic and raised in the Bronx, she is a mother of two and entrepreneur running on public safety, education and small-business themes.

background.text: Earned a high school diploma from Morris High School and an associate degree from Monroe College in 2010.
Career experience includes working as an entrepreneur.
Born in the Dominican Republic and raised in the Bronx; describes her campaign as motivated in part by the death of her nephew, Juan Peña.

priorities.text: Education and youth empowerment: expanding access to quality schools, literacy initiatives and mentorship programs.
Economic growth and opportunity: supporting small businesses and creating pathways to good-paying jobs.
Public safety and youth support: holding repeat violent offenders accountable and investing in youth programs.

positions.summary: Lists holding repeat violent offenders accountable and strengthening public safety among her core campaign priorities.

candidates.researchNotes: Olivo has not completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. She has not previously held elected office, so has no official record. Her campaign website contains templated content unrelated to her candidacy alongside her genuine biography and issue statements; only the material clearly specific to her campaign was used here.

sources.title: Shery Olivo for New York State Assembly District 86

researchNotes: Both Diaz and Olivo advanced to the general election because Diaz won the Republican primary while Olivo held a separate, uncontested Conservative Party line. Diaz has essentially no public footprint beyond her primary win; no website, biography or statements were found for her. None of the three candidates has completed a 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.
